claims.claim: The JCQ deadline for processing access-arrangement applications through Access Arrangements Online for the June 2027 series is 21 March 2027 (modified-paper orders close 31 January 2027), not mid-February; individual centres set their own earlier internal cut-offs.
claims.source_title: Produced on behalf of: ©JCQCIC 2026 Key dates in the examination cycle
claims.key_numbers: AAO applications deadline 21 March 2027; modified papers 31 January 2027
claims.implication: The parent's working assumption of a mid-February AA deadline is wrong in the safe direction, but the real constraint is the centre: a private-candidate centre will want the evidence in hand well before it applies, so the family should treat January 2027 as the date by which the diagnosis letter and documented normal-way-of-working evidence are ready. Add a 'AA evidence pack ready' milestone to the maths and Spanish appendices ahead of the Feb 2027 tier decision.

claims.claim: For a candidate whose need arises from ADHD rather than a learning difficulty, JCQ's extra-time route is Form 9 backed by specialist medical evidence (a letter or report from CAMHS, an HCPC-registered psychologist, a medical consultant, a psychiatrist, or a neurodevelopmental specialist GP / GP with an extended role in ADHD); standardised-score testing by a specialist assessor (the Form 8 route) is not required for ADHD.
claims.source_title: Extra Time in Exams for ADHD: JCQ Rules and How to Apply
claims.authors_year: ADHD Private (secondary guide summarising JCQ AARA), 2025/26
claims.key_numbers: 25% extra time; Form 9; list of acceptable evidence sources shown in search summary; no percentages or scores required
claims.implication: The brief says nothing about the diagnosis paperwork. The single most useful thing the parent can do now is locate (or obtain) a specialist's diagnosis letter that names ADHD and describes its effect on timed work, because without it the Form 9 route is closed. This is a secondary source paraphrasing JCQ; the verifier should check JCQ AARA section 5 / Form 9 wording in the official PDF.

claims.claim: Since the March 2026 update to the 2025-26 JCQ AARA, SENCos must consider and trial supervised rest breaks before applying for 25% extra time for candidates whose impairment is not a learning difficulty, and where extra time is evidenced through Form 9 there must be documented evidence that rest breaks were trialled and found insufficient.
claims.source_title: Produced on behalf of: ©JCQCIC 2026 Changes to the 2025/26 JCQ
claims.key_numbers: 25% extra time; rest-break trial must be documented on Form 9; effective for the 2025-26 edition (the 2026-27 edition was not confirmed in search)
claims.implication: The family should not assume she will get extra time. The realistic first arrangement is supervised rest breaks, and the family needs a paper trail showing breaks were used in timed mocks and whether they were enough. The Dec 2026 and Feb 2027 mocks in the maths appendix are the natural place to run this trial, but the tracker currently records no breaks, session length or 'ran out of time' outcome, so there is nothing to show a SENCo.

claims.claim: Form 8 Part 1 must now contain, as a minimum, teacher feedback and evidence of the candidate's normal way of working, and a 'skeleton' Part 1 is no longer acceptable; for 25% extra time via Form 8 the centre needs samples of internal tests or mock papers showing 25% extra time actually applied plus comments from teaching staff on why it is needed.
claims.source_title: Candidate’s name JCQ/AA/LD Form 8 © JCQ 2025 – Effective from 1 September 2025
claims.key_numbers: Form 8 effective 1 September 2025; 25% extra time; sample count not shown in search summary
claims.implication: Whatever route is used, the centre will want dated, timed evidence. The gcse-maths-marker and gcse-progress-tracker skills should record for every timed paper: the time allowed, whether extra time or breaks were used, and how many marks were lost to unfinished questions, so that mock records can be handed to a SENCo as 'samples of timed work' rather than reconstructed from free-text summaries.

claims.claim: JCQ's guidance for centres accepting private candidates says the SENCo must make clear that the picture of need and normal way of working relates to a private candidate, and may draw on online feedback given to the candidate while studying and on reported difficulties from regular 1:1 tuition.
claims.source_title: Produced on behalf of: ©JCQCIC 2025 An overview of the access arrangements and
claims.implication: This is the hook for the whole system: Claude's session logs and the parent's oversight notes are exactly the '1:1 tuition' evidence JCQ names. The tracker's export_markdown could produce a dated 'normal way of working' report (breaks taken, prompts given, time-outs, unfinished questions) for the SENCo; at present those facts live only in unstructured session summaries and topic 'watch' notes.

claims.claim: Supervised rest breaks are centre-delegated: no Access Arrangements Online application is needed, but for GCSE the SENCo must complete the statement in Part 1 of Form 8 or Form 9 confirming the need, the nature of the impairment, and that rest breaks reflect the candidate's normal way of working within the centre.
claims.source_title: Access Arrangements and Reasonable Adjustments Adjustments for candidates with
claims.key_numbers: no AAO application; statement required in Form 8/9 Part 1; break length not shown in search summary
claims.implication: Rest breaks are the cheapest arrangement to secure and the one JCQ now expects first for ADHD. The maths-tutor-session skill already says 'if frustrated pause and suggest a break'; it should instead build scheduled, logged breaks into timed practice and mocks so that by Dec 2026 there is a record showing breaks are her normal way of working.

claims.claim: A prompter is centre-delegated and may be permitted by the SENCo where a candidate has a substantial, long-term impairment causing persistent distractibility or significant difficulty concentrating (little or no sense of time, loses concentration easily); JCQ's own worked example is a candidate with ADHD for whom supervised rest breaks plus a prompter who may physically point to where she was working are reasonable adjustments.
claims.source_title: Access Arrangements and Reasonable Adjustments – Joint Council for Qualifications
claims.key_numbers: not shown in search summary (criteria are qualitative)
claims.implication: The session logs already show behaviour a prompter addresses (questions not submitted before the session ended, answering more than was asked, drifting into prose). The parent can ask the centre for a prompter with no AAO application, but only if it is her normal way of working, so timed practice at home should include an explicit 'time check / move on' prompt and the tracker should note when it was needed.

claims.claim: A word processor (spelling and grammar check disabled) is centre-delegated with no AAO application where it is the candidate's normal way of working within the centre, including in internal and mock exams from Year 11 upwards, and each centre must have its own word-processor policy.
claims.source_title: Access Arrangements and Reasonable Adjustments – Joint Council for Qualifications
claims.implication: Low priority for this family: AQA 8300 maths is handwritten working and 8692 writing is short; a word processor would help only if handwriting speed were the barrier, and the current tracker shows nothing about handwriting. Do not chase it unless the Spanish writing paper practice shows legibility or speed problems.

claims.claim: Separate invigilation within the centre is a SENDCO decision that must reflect the candidate's normal way of working in internal tests and mocks as a consequence of a long-term medical condition or long-term social, mental or emotional needs, with medical evidence or evidence of ongoing professional support where applicable; nervousness or low-level exam anxiety is not sufficient.
claims.source_title: Access Arrangements and Reasonable Adjustments – Joint Council for Qualifications
claims.implication: A 13-year-old private candidate in a hall of 16-year-olds is a real distraction risk, and many private-candidate centres run small rooms anyway. Ask the chosen centre how private candidates are roomed before deciding whether a formal separate-invigilation arrangement (which needs the ADHD evidence plus normal-way-of-working records) is worth pursuing.

claims.claim: AQA states GCSE Spanish 8692 is available to private candidates, and its private-candidate NEA policy says centres must provide the opportunity for all candidates, including private candidates, to complete NEA and must only accept a private-candidate entry if they are willing to do so; the speaking test is conducted by the centre's teacher in a window timetabled for April and May and assessed by AQA examiners.
claims.key_numbers: speaking window April–May 2027; teacher may open materials up to 3 working days before the test period; 8692/SH June 2027 NEA deadline set by the centre
claims.implication: Spanish entry stands or falls on finding a centre willing to conduct the 8692 speaking test for an external candidate, and that must be confirmed before the Feb 2027 entry deadline, not after. Note the speaking test will happen in April–May 2027, before the maths papers (from 14 May) and well before the Spanish written papers (9 June), so the Spanish appendix's checkpoints need a speaking-ready date around March 2027.

claims.claim: AQA's late-entry fee is 100% of the entry fee on top of the entry fee (2x) and its very-late fee is 150% on top (2.5x); the official AQA June 2027 GCSE entry deadline was not shown in the search summaries, while one London private-candidate centre publishes its own cut-off of 4pm on 1 February 2027 at £290 per subject, rising to £425 after that.
claims.key_numbers: late +100%, very late +150%; example centre £290 on time / £425 late, deadline 1 Feb 2027 (David Game College, https://www.davidgamecollege.com/exam-centre/gcse-entries); AQA 21 Feb 2027 date not shown in search summary
claims.implication: The maths appendix's 'entries close ~21 Feb 2027' is the board date; the centre's own date can be weeks earlier, so the Feb 2027 Higher-mock tier decision should be moved before the centre's cut-off, and the dashboard countdown should show the centre deadline, not just the exam date. Budget roughly £250-£300 per subject plus any centre access-arrangement fee.

claims.claim: AQA and JCQ both publish tools for private candidates to find a centre (AQA's private-candidates page and news guide, JCQ's centre-finder list), but JCQ warns that some listed centres no longer accept private candidates and others are missing, so details must be confirmed directly with the centre; no formal 'exam centre association' was found, only commercial networks such as Tutors & Exams and the HE Exams wiki's advice to ask local home educators.
claims.source_title: Private candidates – Joint Council for Qualifications
claims.key_numbers: not shown in search summary; AQA guide: https://www.aqa.org.uk/news/private-candidates-how-to-find-school-college-exam-centre-this-summer ; AQA page: https://www.aqa.org.uk/student-and-parent-support/private-candidates
claims.implication: Centre choice is the gating task for both subjects and needs three yes answers from one centre: accepts private candidates for 8300, will conduct the 8692 speaking test, and will process ADHD access arrangements for an external candidate. Start in autumn 2026 because a centre that agrees to all three will want the evidence pack early.

claims.claim: There is no minimum age for sitting a GCSE; home-education guidance sites state candidates can start GCSEs at any age, and the only age rule seen is that November-series entries for GCSE English language and maths are restricted to candidates aged 16 and over.
claims.source_title: GCSEs for Home Educators – Home Education in the UK
claims.key_numbers: no minimum age; November series 16+ for English language and maths (source of that line not attributed in search summary)
claims.implication: A 13-year-old can be entered for June 2027. The consequence the parent may not have planned for is the other way round: if the maths grade is below target in June 2027 she cannot use the November 2027 resit series (she will be 14), so the next attempt would be June 2028; that raises the value of the Foundation/Higher tier decision being conservative.

claims.claim: The Patoss/JCQ assessment guidance updated for 2025-26 requires Form 8 Part 1 (teacher feedback and normal way of working) to be completed before any specialist assessment takes place, whether by a centre-based assessor or an external assessor approved by the head of centre, so a privately commissioned assessment done before a centre is engaged may not be accepted on its own.
claims.source_title: Assessing the need for Access Arrangements in Examinations – Joint Council for Qualifications
claims.authors_year: JCQ / Patoss, 2025-26 update to the 7th edition
claims.implication: Do not pay for a private educational-psychologist assessment before a centre is chosen: the centre's SENCo must own Part 1 and approve any external assessor. For ADHD the medical route (C2) is the priority anyway; an assessor's report would only be needed if the centre wants standardised processing-speed evidence.

caveats: Web search budget was exhausted after 17 completed searches; three planned searches were refused (JCQ Form 9 wording for ADHD, existence of a 2026-27 AARA edition effective 1 September 2026, and AQA MFL-specific private-candidate speaking guidance). All claims rest on search-result summaries, not on reading the documents.

The edition of JCQ AARA that will govern summer 2027 is the 2026-27 edition (effective 1 September 2026); only the 2025-26 edition with its March 2026 update was visible. Rules on rest-break trials before extra time (C3) should be re-checked against the 2026-27 text.

C2 (Form 9 route and acceptable evidence sources for ADHD) comes from a secondary guide; the JCQ AARA PDF appeared in the same results but the summary did not attribute the Form 9 text to it. Treat as needing verification against JCQ AARA section 5.

The task brief's 'about 21 February 2027' AQA entry deadline and 'mid-February' AA deadline were not confirmed; JCQ's own key-dates document gives 21 March 2027 for AAO applications, and the AQA entry deadline was not shown in any summary.

No gov.uk or Ofqual page explicitly stating 'no minimum age' appeared in search summaries; C13 relies on home-education guidance sites. The '16+ for November English/maths' rule appeared unattributed in a summary.
No 'exam centre association' was found; the search returned only commercial private-candidate centre networks and JCQ/AQA finder pages.

adhd_specific is mapped for policy documents as: 'direct' where the JCQ text explicitly addresses ADHD (C2, C7), 'indirect' where it addresses non-learning-difficulty impairments generally, 'general' for logistics. None of these are studies.
Centre-specific fees (£290/£425) are one London centre's 2027 prices and not representative of all centres.
